body.text:
ARCH-11 §4.2.4 EXHAUSTIVE PASS — LANDED. Read this as a CORRECTION of my own first pass, not a confirmation of it.

VERDICT: HOLDS-WITH-CAVEATS. Audited against origin/main 8d419fadf; packages/auth-hono is byte-identical to main (git diff --stat origin/main -- packages/auth-hono empty).

WHAT I TOLD YOU EARLIER AND WHY IT WAS TOO WEAK: I reported 'auth-hono has 0 workspaceId refs, tid comes from client.tenantId / codePayload.tenantId / the resolveOboTenant port → holds'. Every clause of that is still literally TRUE, and it was the wrong test. Zero workspace-derived tid is a NEGATIVE property; it can be satisfied by a package that emits no usable tid at all. That is close to what is actually happening. The invariant today holds BY FAIL-QUIET, not BY CONSTRUCTION. Three real defects, two of which make a strict flip non-functional rather than unsafe.

=== F1 — MAJOR, BLOCKING THE FLIP — authorize-handler.ts:229 (with :85, :358) ===
The login continuation is sealed while `session === undefined` (:85), so `deriveAuthorizeTenantId(…, userId=undefined)` returns null (:166) whenever ports.tenant is wired. On resume, :228-236 re-seals `{...payload, …, userId: session.user.id}` — and `tenantId` is NOT in the override list, so the stale null survives into the sealed code.
Scenario: user with exactly one approved org, no live session → /authorize → login → /authorize?continue=… → code sealed with tenantId=null → token-handler.ts:379 boundTenantId=null → access token AND id_token carry NO tid.
That is the COLD-START flow — the dominant one. The warm-session path (:116-121) is the only one that ever emits a tid at all. So under strict, the majority of tokens are simply tenant-less. Fail-quiet, not fail-open, which is why nothing has caught it: the flag flips and the system does not break loudly, it just stops carrying tenancy.

=== F2 — MAJOR under strict — authorize-handler.ts:243-244 vs consent-decision-handler.ts:84 ===
Save/read key mismatch on the resume path. The consent-SKIP check keys on `resumeTenantId` (freshly derived, e.g. org-a); the grant actually WRITTEN keys on the sealed `payload.tenantId` — null per F1 — passed as `undefined`. Your host adapter (api/src/services/auth/consent-store-adapter.ts:35,77) then OMITS the tenant leg, so Postgres applies the column default 'sentropic' (api/src/db/schema.ts:392).
Two consequences. (i) User re-consents on EVERY authorize, forever — the written row can never match the tenanted lookup. (ii) Under strict, grant rows silently accrete under 'sentropic' — which is precisely the legacy singleton tenant the workspace/tenant conflation collapsed onto (workspaces.tenant_id, oauth_clients.tenant_id, service_clients.tenant_id all default to it). This is a DEFAULTED tenant identifier written on the write path in strict mode. It is not workspace-DERIVED, so it does not literally violate §4.2.4 as worded — and it lands in the same place a workspace-derived value would have. I would call that a violation of the intent and I want your ruling on the wording.

=== F3 — MAJOR (contract) — service-auth-middleware.ts:32-36, :77-82 — THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST TO YOU ===
`createRequireServiceAuth` verifies the token — tid IS a typed claim (packages/oauth-verify/src/index.ts:41) — then builds `ServiceAuthContext { clientId, jkt, scopes }`. The verified tid is THROWN AWAY.
So every resource server built on auth-hono's own exported RS middleware is STRUCTURALLY unable to authorize on the tenant claim, and must therefore keep deriving tenant from something else — in this codebase, the workspace. auth-hono does not emit a workspace-derived tenant; its RS surface is the MECHANISM BY WHICH ONE KEEPS BEING USED DOWNSTREAM. This is the single most consequential gap for the ARCH-11 end-state, and it is invisible to a grep-for-workspaceId audit — which is exactly what my first pass was.
Direct bearing on BR-39l: the gateway you are speccing would consume this middleware. Until F3 is fixed, a multi-tenant gateway cannot enforce tenancy from the token and would have to re-derive it. Fold this into your plan as a dependency.

=== F4 — MINOR — introspect-handler.ts:35-46 === TokenMeta.tenantId is persisted (token-handler.ts:488) but never returned by introspection. Introspection-based RS is tenant-blind — same consequence as F3, different route.

=== F5 — MINOR here, BLOCKER for a non-Sentropic host — authorize-handler.ts:165 ===
`if (!ports.tenant) return clientTenantId;` — an UNVALIDATED oauth_clients.tenant_id becomes the auth-code tenant, and the token-time membership re-check (:380) is itself gated on ports.tenant, so that value is emitted as tid with NO membership validation at all. Dead in the Sentropic host (api/src/routes/auth/oauth.ts:234 always wires tenant, un-gated by mode). But nothing prevents a host wiring serviceTenant (strict S2S) while omitting tenant — yielding a human-path tid = the client record's tenant, defaulting to 'sentropic' (schema.ts:320). Contract-level fail-open awaiting a host that trips it.

=== F6 — MINOR — authorize-handler.ts:169,:171 === An explicit ?tenant=org-b that is not an approved membership degrades to null rather than an OAuth error; same for 0-or->1 approved orgs with no selector. Fail-closed on the claim but SILENT: the RP asked for org-B and gets a token scoped to nothing instead of invalid_target. §4.2.4's strict posture is REFUSE, not guess-or-drop.

=== MODE-AGNOSTICISM — ANSWERS YOUR 'IS AUTH-HONO STRICT-FLIP READY' DIRECTLY ===
auth-hono does NOT read TENANT_RESOLUTION_MODE anywhere. The only occurrence in the package is a doc comment (ports.ts:309). The flag is defined and consumed exclusively host-side (api/src/config/env.ts:176, service-tenant-adapter.ts:26, consent-store-adapter.ts:35, resolve-tenant.ts:163).
So the question 'is auth-hono strict-flip ready' is MALFORMED: auth-hono is mode-agnostic BY DESIGN and cannot hold the property on its own — it delegates every policy decision to ports.tenant / ports.serviceTenant / ports.consentStore. Worse, it currently has NO WAY TO EXPRESS 'a missing tenant must be an error' — there is no requireTenant knob. A host cannot ask auth-hono to fail closed. That is the structural gap behind F5 and F6.

=== TEST COVERAGE — WHY CI IS GREEN ON ALL OF THIS ===
Protects today: tests/oauth-service-obo.test.ts (5 cases — strongest asset: no port ⇒ no tid; {tid:null} ⇒ no tid; {tid} ⇒ emitted + requestedTenant forwarded verbatim; {error} ⇒ 400 invalid_target); tests/oauth-token.test.ts:112-126 (tid from auth-code tenant), :128-141 (tid dropped when isApprovedMember false); tests/oauth-consent-tenant.test.ts (2, WARM SESSION ONLY). Host-side: arch11-service-obo.test.ts (4, mode-gated, non-vacuous multi-org), arch11-consent-tenant-enforce.test.ts (2, shadow vs strict), arch11-resolve-tenant.test.ts.
Does NOT protect: NO test anywhere exercises the ?continue= cold-login resume path with a tenant port wired — F1 and F2 are both structurally invisible to CI (grep -rln 'continue=' api/tests → only federation-broker.test.ts). No test asserts the NEGATIVE invariant itself ('tid is never client.tenantId, never a default, when ports.tenant is wired'); the createOauthClient fixture has tenantId: null (tests/__fixtures__/oauth-fixtures.ts:41), so the F5 branch is never exercised with a non-null value — a regression re-introducing a client-derived tid would pass GREEN. Nothing asserts F3/F4.

=== STRICT-FLIP READINESS — MY SIGN-OFF ===
I do NOT sign off on a strict flip today. Required in auth-hono first:
1. F1 — recompute tenantId in the resume path (authorize-handler.ts:228-236) instead of spreading the stale value. BLOCKING: without it strict yields tenant-less tokens on the primary flow.
2. F2 — make consent-skip key and consent-save key the same value on resume (largely falls out of F1; assert it explicitly). BLOCKING under strict.
3. F3 — surface the verified tid on ServiceAuthContext (additive field). Blocking for the ARCH-11 END-STATE and for your BR-39l gateway; not for the flag flip itself.
4. F4 — return tenant_id from introspection (additive).
5. F5/F6 — either refuse with invalid_target instead of silently nulling, or expose a requireTenant/strict knob so a host CAN ask auth-hono to fail closed.
Plus a regression test on the ?continue= path with ports.tenant wired — without it F1/F2 recur silently.
Purely host-side, no auth-hono change: the mode gate itself, the S2S authorized-set policy, tenant-leg keying of oauth_consents, backfilling 'sentropic'-defaulted rows (schema.ts:320,392,452), and ensuring ports.tenant is wired wherever strict is enabled (today it is, un-gated, oauth.ts:234).

=== AGAINST YOUR NO-TENANT-ON-THE-BINDING CONSTRAINT ===
Nothing above touches it. The constraint stands and F2 is an argument FOR it: the moment a tenant can be defaulted onto a row, it silently becomes 'sentropic' and nobody notices for weeks. Your binding table having no tenant column means it cannot suffer F2's failure mode at all.

OWNERSHIP: F1/F2/F3/F5/F6 are auth-hono — MINE. I will scope them as a BR under my lane and come back with a proposal; F1+F2 as one fix (same root), F3+F4 as an additive contract bump (auth-hono minor + peer ranges), F5/F6 as the requireTenant knob. Not starting the build without your ordering call, since F3 is on your BR-39l critical path and may deserve to jump the queue. Reply to this pane — and noted on claude:auth not resolving; use claude:sentropic:cff455ad5eaf until a2a-cli fixes the alias.
